description: Checkpoint invariants and their falsifiers. A falsifier is a specific mutation of the implementation under which the named test MUST fail. A test that survives its own falsifier cannot fail, and a test that cannot fail proves nothing - so tests/test_falsifiers.py runs each mutation in a subprocess and asserts the target test breaks.
rationale: Adopted at M1.2 after a governing rule adopted mid-project (commutativity, see STATE.md) silently downgraded a planned M1.2 checkpoint from 'proves something' to 'cannot fail'. Nothing would have flagged it; the suite would still have been green. Review habits are documentation. This makes vacuity a red test.
scope: Deliberately limited to properties where the TEST is the sole line of defence. Some checkpoints are also guarded at runtime - build.py raises BuildError when manifest counts disagree with what was written, and the contract replay check catches in-process irreproducibility. Falsifying those would prove the guard works, not the test, so they are listed under not_falsified with the reason.

invariants.asserts: The built index DDL contains zero AUTOINCREMENT and zero CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
invariants.falsifier: Append a table carrying INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT to store.SCHEMA - the shape a plausible future 'build_log' table would take.
invariants.why_this_falsifier: The realistic way this regresses is not someone editing an existing table, but someone adding a new one without thinking about it.

invariants.asserts: The conflict-free union keeps the semantic-analysis confidence/reasoning on the 4 payload-divergent duplicate groups.
invariants.falsifier: Replace collapse_edge_group with the strip-metadata rule - the exact alternative rejected when the collapse rule was chosen.
invariants.why_this_falsifier: Turns a design decision into a permanent discriminator. The test must be able to tell the chosen rule from the runner-up, or it is not testing the decision at all.

invariants.asserts: No dropped edge reappears in the index under a fuzzy-matched endpoint.
invariants.falsifier: Replace normalize.resolve_endpoint with a substring-matching resolver that maps a missing slug onto the first node whose source_ref contains it.
invariants.why_this_falsifier: Three of the four dangling targets have plausible near-matches, so this is the repair someone would actually be tempted to write. It produces a valid-looking index that silently corrupts every traversal crossing the guessed edge.

invariants.asserts: The 5 nodes with no edges remain in the index and stay searchable.
invariants.falsifier: Filter nodes with no incident edge out of normalize_all.
invariants.why_this_falsifier: Dropping them improves every connectivity statistic while silently shrinking the searchable corpus - an attractive change with an invisible cost.

invariants.asserts: The manifest content_hash is identical under PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1 and 12345.
invariants.falsifier: Add node_types as list(set(...)) rather than sorted(set(...)) in manifest.build_content - 25 distinct values, so iteration order genuinely varies.
invariants.why_this_falsifier: Set iteration order varies with the hash seed. This is the single most common way non-determinism enters a build, it is invisible in a single-process run, and this subprocess test is the only thing that catches it.
invariants.registry_finding: The first falsifier here mutated embedding_models and was rejected as a no-op: this corpus has exactly 1 model and 1 dimension, so list(set) equals sorted(set). That is a fact about the corpus - no multi-element set currently reaches content_hash - so the hash-seed test guards a class of bug the present data cannot exhibit on its own.

not_falsified.reason: build.py compares manifest counts against rows actually written and raises BuildError first. A falsifier would prove that guard fires, not this test.
reconcile() is asserted on every build inside build.py, so the runtime guard triggers before the test can.
Enforced by the contract replay check itself; the assertion is a formality after the decorator has already compared results.
